title: Choosing covered calls: IV divided by realized volatility, not IV alone
summary: Selling covered calls or cash-secured puts only on high-IV names is like shorting a stock only because its price is high. You need a valuation ratio, like P/E for stocks. For options, divide implied volatility by realized volatility, your unit of risk, to see if the option is cheap, fair or rich.

steps.caption: A high-IV stock. High IV alone is like a high share price: it says nothing about value.
Implied volatility: the price of the option, quoted in volatility terms.
Realized volatility: the unit of risk, how much the stock really moves.
IV relative to realized works like a P/E ratio. It tells you if the option is cheap, fair or rich.
Rank candidate covered calls by IV over realized, not by IV alone.

takeaways: High IV alone is not a reason to sell an option.
Divide IV by realized volatility to compare options on an equal basis.
Use the ratio to judge cheap, fair or rich, like P/E for stocks.
caveats: VAY (volatility-adjusted yield) is the speaker's own metric, sold through his tools. It is unverified here.
